references.text: Moses reminds the people that the Lord spoke to them face to face on the mountain, out of the fire – a direct parallel to the introduction of the Ten Commandments.
Summarizes that these words the Lord spoke to the entire assembly on the mountain, and confirms that God himself uttered the Ten Commandments.
Describes how the Lord spoke to Israel from the fire and proclaimed his covenant, the Ten Commandments, which he wrote on two stone tablets.
The immediate context before God speaks the Ten Commandments – Moses goes down to the people to prepare them for God's speech.
Moses conveys all the Lord's words to the people, referring back to the commandments God spoke in chapter 20.
Hebrews warns against rejecting the one who speaks from heaven, referencing when God spoke at Sinai and shook the earth.
Stephen's speech mentions that Moses received living words on Mount Sinai to pass on to Israel.
Both verses mark God's direct speech as establishing a new order for humanity after a catastrophe.
Matthew uses the expression 'all these words' to create a clear allusion to the revelation at Sinai and present Jesus' teaching as a new law code.
